text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) will soon undertake a review of its warehousing system, and how independent warehouse companies are.

The Securities and Investments Board (SIB), which reviewed the LME last year after the Sumitomo Corp Corp scandal, recommended that the Exchange should assess the independence of warehouse compaanies and other firms which play a role in the market.
In a notice to members LME Chief Executive David King said the executive and its advisers will be undertaking a review to assess such independence over coming weeks.
The LME also amended some of its regulations regarding large position reporting, non-market price transactions and traded option valuations.

In the case of large position reporting the LME said it intends to provide relevent members with a means of transmitting data electronically by the end of 1997. At present this information is provided to the LME by secure fax.
The LME's traded options committee, meanwhile, has decided to introduce a volatility "wing" on copper Grade A options for clearing valuation purposes at strikes to be determined.
It is doing this because the volatilities for options for strikes other than at-the-money have been differing recently.
All members who submit volatility quotes to the LME on a daily basis must now notify the Executive if volatilities are significantly different for strikes other than those at-the-money, it said.
